transcript:
Meeting: Zephyr Smart Retail — POC budgeting, batching & benchmark scope
Date: 2026-09-29 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Morgan Blake (Redwood AE); Priya Shah (Redwood SE); Liam Chen (Zephyr DS); Nora Alvarez (Zephyr CTO); Samir Patel (Zephyr Platform)

[00:00] Morgan: alright everyone, um thanks for joining. quick intro — i'm Morgan, AE here at Redwood. with me is Priya, our solutions engineer. we're planning a short pilot to help you validate unit economics and latency tradeoffs, right?
[00:18] Liam: yeah hi all. thanks, we've been looking at a few vendors but main thing for us is understanding per-token cost at scale and the latency impact when we enable batching, caching, and quantization.
[00:30] Priya: perfect, that's what we'll scope. real quick, can you walk through the workload? what does a session look like for Zephyr?
[00:40] Nora: sure — casual overview, our in-store assistant takes about 3 to 8 back-and-forth messages, average input length 120 tokens, output ~220 tokens. peak concurrent sessions around 400 during promos, baseline closer to 80.
[00:58] Samir: and important constraint: everything must run in our VPC — we need private deployment or dedicated capacity. also KMS integration for keys.
[01:10] Priya: got it. so two deployment paths — Redwood Dedicated or Private. Dedicated gives predictable throughput, Private gives complete network control. both support KMS and audit logs.
[01:26] Morgan: success metrics — what are you aiming for? 
[01:29] Liam: p95 latency under 200ms for short requests, ideally < 150ms for quick prompts. cost-wise, our finance target is sub-$0.04 per 1k input+output tokens, at projected volumes.
[01:45] Priya: ok interesting. quick framing: per-token econ depends a lot on batching window, sequence length, and whether you can leverage KV caching for repeated prefixes. with your avg output 220 tokens, batching could help a lot but will add tail latency if you increase window.
[02:04] Morgan: and quantization — we can evaluate int8/in4 variants to reduce GPU utilization; that moves the per-token compute cost down but sometimes impacts quality.
[02:14] Nora: quality is non-negotiable for the assistant. small hallucination rate is okay but if generation loses brand voice it's a problem.
[02:23] Priya: we'll include a quality reg check tied to canonical prompts in the benchmark.
[02:30] Liam: curious about numbers — ballpark per-token on Redwood hosted vs dedicated?
[02:36] Morgan: rough yes: hosted API — higher per-token list but lowest setup friction. Dedicated — lower per-token at committed capacity, especially if you use continuous batching and quantized kernels. in a pilot, we do both: run a dedicated-like workload on our infra to simulate per-token at scale.
[02:53] Priya: to make this tangible, we'll run two benchmarks: 1) latency-focused: simulate 400 concurrent sessions with small batching window (<=10ms) to measure p50/p95; 2) cost-focused: run a throughput run with larger batching to measure tokens/sec and estimate $ per 1k tokens across model variants and quantization.
[03:15] Samir: when you say batching window <=10ms what does that mean operationally? are we queuing requests?
[03:21] Priya: yes, batching window is the amount of time we wait to accumulate requests before dispatching a batch. small window favors latency but gives smaller batch sizes. Redwood runtime also supports continuous batching where we pack requests aggressively without adding a lot of extra latency, but it depends on traffic shape.
[03:38] Liam: and KV cache? our use case has repeated prompts: product catalog lookups, etc.
[03:44] Priya: KV cache stores key-value activations for autoregressive generation so if you have repeated prefixes across sessions, you can avoid recomputing the prefix. that can cut compute per token by 20-60% depending on overlap. note: cache hit rates are workload dependent.
[03:58] Nora: can you replicate that in the benchmark run?
[04:01] Priya: yes — please provide a sample of canonical prompts; we'll run synthetic sessions that reproduce the prefix repetition and measure cache hit rate.
[04:12] Morgan: timeline — proposed pilot is 4 weeks: week 0 — prep and env docs, week 1 — baseline latency benchmark, week 2 — throughput/cost benchmarking with batching/quantization matrix, week 3 — analyze results, tie to cost model and executive summary.
[04:29] Liam: that works. what about success criteria to decide go/no-go?
[04:33] Morgan: how about a combination: 1) p95 latency < 200ms in latency-focused benchmark; 2) estimated cost <= $0.04 per 1k tokens at your projected 2M monthly tokens after applying caching/quantization; 3) quality regression under 2% on canonical prompts.
[04:50] Nora: we can accept p95 at 200ms but prefer <150. finance will push on the 0.04 threshold.
[04:57] Priya: we'll parameterize the cost model so you can play with savings from caching hit rate (0-60%) and batching windows. we'll deliver a worksheet with sensitivity analysis.
[05:08] Samir: security note — we need SAML/SSO for console access and audit logs forwarded to our ELK stack. can you do that?
[05:15] Morgan: yes, Redwood supports SAML, RBAC, and audit log export; for Private we'll show the log forwarding topology. we'll attach SOC2 and network diagrams to the SOW.
[05:26] Liam: curious re: fallback behavior — if capacity spikes, can requests fall back to a cheaper model or degrade gracefully?
[05:33] Priya: yes, smart routing policies can fall back to a smaller model or to a cached response; you'll configure per-route fallbacks. part of the analysis will show cost/latency tradeoffs for those modes.
[05:45] Morgan: ok let's get nitty-gritty on the benchmark matrix — which models to test?
[05:50] Liam: we want a high-quality base model and a faster cheaper variant. maybe base = Llama-3-70B-ish equivalent; fast = 13B quantized.
[05:59] Priya: great. matrix: baseline (fp16 big model, no quant), int8 quantized big model, 13B int4, and a cached run for each. measure tokens/sec, avg token compute ms, GPU utilization, and p50/p95 latencies.
[06:13] Nora: for the quality checks, we'll have 30 canonical prompts and a small human review panel; automated metrics should include exact match for entity extraction tasks.
[06:23] Priya: perfect, we'll wire the quality hooks into the benchmark harness.
[06:27] Morgan: sample estimates — these are illustrative: with no caching and small batch window, cost might be around $0.06 per 1k tokens on a big model. with aggressive caching and int8, you could get to $0.02-0.03 per 1k. again these vary.
[06:44] Liam: that's helpful. finance will want the sensitivity table.
[06:48] Samir: do you have an expectation for infra sizing — GPUs and networking — for the dedicated pool to hit our peaks?
[06:55] Priya: we need more precise qps and token distribution but very roughly, for 400 concurrent sessions and average throughput ~1 request per session every 30s, you'd need X A100-equivalent GPUs. we'll give a sizing table after we see real traffic.
[07:10] Nora: can you run an initial synthetic run that mirrors our traffic curve during a promo window? that's the most important scenario.
[07:17] Priya: yes, please provide the traffic curve and we'll craft the synthetic driver.
[07:22] Morgan: closing — next steps recap: we (Redwood) will send pilot SOW, cost worksheet, SOC2 + topology. Zephyr will share canonical prompts, 2 weeks of anonymized logs, and the promo traffic curve. then schedule benchmark run for week of Oct 5.
[07:39] Liam: sounds good. question — commercial terms: is there a minimum commit for Dedicated pilot?
[07:44] Morgan: pilots are flexible; for Dedicated proof-of-econ we typically ask for a short reserved window to get realistic numbers, but we can run an isolated benchmark in our infra if you prefer no commit. we'll outline options in the SOW.
[07:58] Nora: ok let's do the no-commit benchmark first. if results look good we'll discuss a shorter reserved commit.
[08:05] Priya: action items again — i'll draft the benchmark plan and include the caching scenarios and quantization matrix. Morgan will send pricing worksheet. Samir and Liam will share logs and traffic curve.
[08:16] Samir: note on networking — our infra does egress filter rules tightly, so when you send the topology we'll validate with our network team.
[08:24] Morgan: absolutely, we'll include IP ranges and flow diagrams.
[08:28] Liam: thanks all, appreciate the clarity.
[08:31] Morgan: thanks everyone — we'll follow up with docs and a calendar invite for the benchmark kickoff.
[08:36] End of call.
file_notes: Transcription includes a few ASR errors (e.g., 'K-V cash' for KV cache in places). Voices overlap briefly at 05:26-05:33. This file is the POC scoping call focused on cost/unit econ and benchmarks.
